title: Foundations - Lesson 3 - Anthropology
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Unity of Mankind
subpoints: All humanity descends from Adam and Eve
Acts 17:26 affirms one blood/origin for all nations
Scientific law of uniformity supports common genetic origin
Rejection of racial superiority and the concept of multiple races

outline.title: The Nature of Racism and Sin
subpoints: Racism is a heinous sin akin to abortion
It presupposes that some humans are less than fully human
Biblical anthropology rejects any basis for ethnic hierarchy

outline.title: Self-Knowledge Through Scripture
subpoints: Modern anthropology seeks self-knowledge via psychology, sociology, and metaphysics
Reformed theology asserts self-knowledge is only possible through knowledge of God
James 1 describes the Word of God as a mirror for true self-reflection
Critique of existentialism and inward-looking self-discovery

outline.title: The Image of God (Imago Dei)
subpoints: Genesis 1:26-27 establishes humanity's creation in God's image
The image includes dominion over creation
The Fall distorted this image, leading to the suppression of truth

summary:
This lesson, the third in the Foundations series, explores the Reformed doctrine of anthropology, or the study of humanity. The sermon begins by establishing the biblical unity of all mankind, citing Acts 17:26 to demonstrate that all nations descend from one blood or one man. This theological truth is reinforced by the scientific law of uniformity, which suggests that the genetic diversity of all ethnicities was contained within the first humans, Adam and Eve. Consequently, the sermon argues that the concept of racial superiority is biblically and scientifically unfounded, identifying racism as a grave sin that denies the full humanity of others, similar in nature to the sin of abortion.

The discussion then shifts to the question of self-knowledge. While modern anthropology attempts to understand humanity through psychology, sociology, and metaphysics, Reformed theology asserts that true self-knowledge is only attainable through the knowledge of God and His Word. Using James 1 as a reference, the sermon illustrates that Scripture acts as a mirror, allowing individuals to see their true condition. This perspective critiques existentialist philosophies that rely solely on internal introspection, which are described as insufficient and potentially destructive.

Finally, the sermon addresses the doctrine of the Imago Dei, or the image of God. Citing Genesis 1:26-27, it affirms that humanity was created in God's image and given dominion over the earth. However, the Fall introduced a distortion to this image, as described in Romans 1, where humanity suppressed the truth and exchanged it for lies. This section sets the stage for understanding how the original sin affects human nature and the necessity of redemption through Christ.
